summary.text: A 36-year-old male-to-female transgender patient with a past record of AIDS was referred to the Plastic Surgery Division with a six-month history of genital lymphedema. She had received chemotherapy and 12 radiotherapy sessions for anal canal epidermoid carcinoma, the radiotherapy finishing one year before presentation, with clinically complete remission.

She then presented with inguinal swelling and pain, local edema and erythema, without fever, and relapse was suspected. CT, PET and MRI showed nodules, lymph node enlargement, a hypermetabolic subcutaneous area and scrotal edema. Afterwards she revealed earlier liquid silicone injections to the buttocks and thighs for esthetic purposes. No sign of recurrent malignancy was found and she was referred for plastic surgery and urology consultations.

Initial examination showed significant scrotal enlargement with erythematous tender infiltrated skin, non-palpable testicles and loss of penile shaft contour. After multispecialty discussion the affected scrotal tissue was excised, preserving the penis and testicles, with primary closure and no scrotal reconstruction as the patient wished. Histopathology showed chronic lymphedema with lipoblast-like cells that were CD68 positive and S100 negative.

The postoperative period was mostly uneventful apart from minor dehiscence of the superficial wound in the ventral penis, managed with dressings. The result was considered satisfactory by the patient and surgical team, with no signs of lymphedema relapse after nearly one year of follow-up.

ambiguities.issue: The discussion states the scrotal lymphedema was "probably caused by radiotherapy" and that liquid silicone was "also a contributory factor". The cause is hedged and is not recorded as an asserted cause in any fact.

evidence.quote: In the present case, the patient presented acquired scrotal lymphedema, probably caused by radiotherapy. The presence of liquid silicone in the subcutaneous tissue and pelvic lymph nodes was also a contributory factor.

ambiguities.must_not_infer: Do not infer that radiotherapy or silicone is the established cause.

ambiguities.issue: The planned reconstruction names two alternatives (skin grafts or local thigh flaps); neither is asserted, and the source later says there was no need for either.

evidence.quote: to reconstruct the perineal defect with skin grafts or local thigh flaps

ambiguities.must_not_infer: Do not infer that a graft or flap reconstruction was planned as a specific method or performed.

ambiguities.issue: Follow-up is "nearly one year" in the text and "10-month" in the Figure 6 caption. These are not two values for one stated measurement (the caption dates the photographed result; the text gives the follow-up length), so this is an ambiguity, not a source conflict; both are kept as separate facts and events.

ambiguities.must_not_infer: Do not equate the presentations or order the CT, PET and MRI against the referral.

ambiguities.issue: The only sex wording is the pronoun "She"; the article calls the patient male-to-female transgender and does not state sex assigned at birth. The pronoun reflects gender identity, so documented_sex (female) is kept review_only and only the documented gender identity is accepted.

ambiguities.must_not_infer: Do not infer documented sex or sex assigned at birth from the pronoun, the transgender label, the anatomy or the photographs.

ambiguities.issue: The PET focal hypermetabolic area is only "probably" a lymph node, and the lipoblast-like cells "could be explained" by phagocytized silicone; both are hedged and kept hedged.

ambiguities.must_not_infer: Do not assert the lymph node identification or the silicone explanation.

ambiguities.issue: Discussion sentences b00021 refer literally to this patient ("Because the patient is male-to-female transgender, she considered...") and to her single operation, but carry no time; they are kept as untimed facts and are not linked to the nearly-one-year follow-up event.

evidence.quote: Local reconstruction was achieved by means of primary closure in a single operation, without erectile dysfunction or impairment of penile sensitivity.

ambiguities.must_not_infer: Do not assign a follow-up time to these statements or attach them to a timed event.

ambiguities.issue: Granulomas appear only in the abstract summary of the radiological findings; the body text does not describe them.
